video_title: James Harden Is 37 and Struggling: Can He Turn It Around? | Chris Mannix & Grant Liffmann

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix evaluates the Cleveland Cavaliers' early season performance
quotes.excerpt: The Cavs looked like conference contenders in that game.
quotes.quote: If everybody had gone to bed for the first two weeks, only watched the New York Knicks game on Wednesday night, they would have understood why. The Cavs looked like conference contenders in that game. James Harden goes for 32 points, shoots 64% from the floor, Donovan Mitchell a nice tidy 23, Jared Allen has a double-double. A couple of young guys getting 30-ish points off the bench, the defense makes big stops, Peyton Watson chase-down block on Duane McBride. It's like, well, they went to the Garden and won, like they got a little bit of vengeance for what happened to the conference finals last year. Alas, that was an outlier in what's been going on on the Cavaliers this season.
quotes.social_post: Chris Mannix says the Cavaliers looked like true conference contenders in their win against the Knicks, but notes that performance was an outlier in what has otherwise been a disappointing start to the season.

quotes.speaker: Grant Liffmann
quotes.summary_phrase: Grant Liffmann and Chris Mannix debate the Cavaliers' playoff potential
quotes.excerpt: I don't think they're built for the playoffs and I think we've seen it.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Your thoughts now? Are you buying or selling the Cavs still as a conference contender?

text_blocks.speaker: Grant Liffmann
text_blocks.text: So let me ask you this. You said the bullish part, but I want to make this clear. I was bullish on them in the regular season. And there is a, and I'm still going to put that caveat there. So when you say conference contender, are you talking conference the regular season or are you talking playoffs?

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I mean, I, so how I would call conference contender would be they can win the conference, not in the regular season, win, advance to the finals, basically.

text_blocks.speaker: Grant Liffmann
text_blocks.text: Yeah, so no. And I, and I actually wasn't in on them before the season either on that. I just don't, I don't think they're built for the playoffs and I think we've seen it. These, these players, it just, it hasn't worked. And I don't know why it would have changed this year.

quotes.social_post: Grant Liffmann and Chris Mannix agree that the Cavaliers are not built for a deep playoff run. Liffmann says he is selling the team as a conference contender because the current roster construction simply has not worked.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix questions if James Harden's struggles are permanent
quotes.excerpt: What we're seeing from James Harden, is this permanent or is this a blip?
quotes.quote: What we're seeing from James Harden, is this permanent or is this a blip? James Harden historically has been a phenomenal regular season player. And when he's slowed down, has often come either in the playoffs for sure, or late in the regular season when all the minutes he plays and all the bumps he takes catches up to him. We're in week three right now of the regular season and James Harden's numbers across the board have been awful. He's I think still sub-40% from the floor, sub-40% from three-point range, scoring numbers are the lowest I think since his rookie year. I mean, all these numbers are like you had to go back to very early Oklahoma City days to see numbers like this from James Harden.
quotes.social_post: Chris Mannix questions if James Harden's early season struggles are permanent, noting that his shooting percentages are currently at the lowest levels seen since his rookie season in Oklahoma City.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix praises James Harden's ability to secure contracts
quotes.excerpt: James Harden is the greatest businessman in the history of the game.
quotes.quote: James Harden is the greatest businessman in the history of the game. He is the greatest. I have never in my life never covered a player that is as good about getting what he wants, both in terms of location and money than James Harden. James Harden gets what James Harden wants. He's got a three-year deal worth nearly $100 million and the back end of that deal is a player option. So you can't convince me, Grant, that when year two is up, he's not going to be able to figure out a way to get like two extra years from the Cavaliers. He's going to be playing like he's going to be 46, still getting two-year extension with player options. It's crazy. This guy is a genius.
quotes.social_post: Chris Mannix calls James Harden the greatest businessman in NBA history, arguing that no player is better at securing both his preferred location and massive contracts than Harden.

quotes.speaker: Grant Liffmann
quotes.summary_phrase: Grant Liffmann analyzes the decline of high-scoring NBA stars
quotes.excerpt: They can keep on putting up numbers later, but all of a sudden their impact on winning goes away.
quotes.quote: It used to be certain players when they hit a wall, they're just done. But I think what we've seen recently, a lot of these high-scorers, good players, they can keep on putting up numbers later, but all of a sudden their impact on winning goes away. And I want to give an example of like DeMar DeRozan for instance. When he's out there, DeMar DeRozan is still unbelievably skilled. He can put up 20 a game, but somehow his impact on winning goes away, right? And I think that's what you look for with a James Harden. He may get his numbers back and stuff, and maybe that'll impact winning. Like he has done his entire career. Let's give credit to James Harden. He is one of the best regular season winners ever.
quotes.social_post: Grant Liffmann discusses the decline of high-scoring stars, noting that players like DeMar DeRozan can still put up numbers, but their overall impact on winning often diminishes as they age.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix critiques the Cavaliers' defensive and offensive issues
quotes.excerpt: They've got to get better overall defensively, Harden and Mitchell point of attack defense is a problem.
quotes.quote: They've got to get better overall defensively, Harden and Mitchell point of attack defense is a problem. Evan Mobley is numbers are fine, but Grant, like Evan Mobley's got to be able to create his own shot for that team to succeed in the playoffs. I was watching him kind of try to back down Josh Hart on Wednesday. You got to be able to back down Josh Hart, man. I know Josh is a strong guy, but Josh is a tweener forward. You're supposed to be a de facto center, and you got to be able to put your shoulder down and get into the paint against Josh Hart. I like that Mobley's making some shots, but he's got to be able to create his own shot for this team to have success.
quotes.social_post: Chris Mannix says Evan Mobley must improve his ability to create his own shot, specifically pointing out that he needs to be able to back down smaller defenders like Josh Hart for the Cavaliers to succeed.
